title: BF16-embedding control arm (closes audit blocker D4)
purpose: The audit found that no arm in the trellis embedding study had a same-harness, same-env BF16 control. Every comparison crossed a harness boundary, a checkpoint boundary, or both, and several claimed effects were smaller than this repo's own demonstrated 0.94% kernel-routing noise band. This receipt supplies the missing control.
method: Constructed an identity pre-encoded embedding file (the unmodified BF16 embed_tokens weight with a bits=16 marker) so the injection step is a no-op copy. Everything else - capture env, kernel routing, KV dtype, eager mode, batching, and the canonical fidelity.py replay - is byte-identical to the K4/K6/K8 arms. The only variable across the four arms is the embedding itself.
replay_tool: canonical fidelity.py replay (same tool as the K4/K6/K8 arms)

one_variable_comparison.note: All four arms: same harness, same checkpoint, same env, only the embedding differs.
one_variable_comparison.noise_band: 0.94%, established by this repo's own frontier-2026-08-19.md: the identical checkpoint on the identical profile measured 0.003412 / 0.003407 / 0.003437 / 0.003405 as kernel routing changed, with no quantizer change.

conclusions: Trellis K8 embeddings are fidelity-neutral: +0.17% against the control, well inside the 0.94% noise band and therefore not a resolvable effect.
Trellis K6 embeddings are also fidelity-neutral: +0.69%, inside the noise band.
Trellis K4 is the only arm with a resolvable cost: +7.87% mean and +10.14% p99 against the control. This is 8x the noise band and is a real effect.
The correct claim for K6/K8 is 'fidelity-neutral', not 'better than BF16'. Both are slightly ABOVE the control, as physics requires - a lossy embedding cannot improve on an exact one.

The previously published claim that trellis K6 (0.002667) beat BF16 embeddings (0.002700) is now dead. That 0.002700 figure was an OFFLINE number from a different harness; the true same-harness BF16 control is 0.0026488, which is 1.89% below it. K6 is slightly worse than the real control, not better than it.

Every sub-1% superiority claim in the original embedding receipt is retracted: K8-vs-K6 (0.53%), K6-vs-BF16 (1.22% as previously computed), and the p99 orderings among K6/K8 and the control (spread 0.8%) are all inside the noise band.
what_this_does_not_settle: The int6/int8 comparators remain uncontrolled: they were measured on the strength-zero R30 checkpoint with fidelity_gate.py, not on K5K6-hydrated with fidelity.py replay. This control does not make those comparable.

The trellis round-trip in these arms saves no memory - it dequantizes back to BF16. The production embedding path is per-row packed int6 (VLLM_EXL3_EMBED_ONLINE_BITS=6), which is a different scheme and is not measured here.
Whether the production packed-int6 embedding is fidelity-neutral against this control remains unmeasured.
closes: Audit blocker D4 (no matched control) from receipts/trellis-audit-corrections-2026-08-22.json.
